tools.description: Close a named session. A background session's command is signalled on the host (INT, then TERM, then KILL) before its channel is dropped; an interactive session's shell is ended. The response says so if the command could not be signalled or had not stopped in time.
tools.name: close-session

tools.description: List all configured SSH profiles and their connection status. Use this to discover available hosts before running commands.
tools.name: list-connections

tools.description: List active sessions for a given SSH profile.
tools.name: list-sessions

tools.description: Open a named session on a remote host. Use type="interactive" for stateful shell (CWD/env persists between commands) or type="background" for long-running processes.

name.description: Session name (alphanumeric, dash, underscore, max 64 chars)

tools.name: open-session

tools.description: Execute a command with sudo elevation. Goes through the approval gate; approvalPolicy on the profile decides whether that is a prompt, an automatic allow, or a refusal. The sudo password is piped via stdin (never visible in process list). Single-line only: a command containing a line break is refused, so upload a multi-line script with sftp-upload and run it by path.
tools.name: privileged-command

tools.description: Execute a READ-ONLY command from an allowlist (ls, cat, grep, find, stat, df, etc.). This tool does NOT modify the system. Prefer this tool for all read operations. Single-line only: a command containing a line break is refused, so upload a multi-line script with sftp-upload and run it by path.

command.description: Read-only shell command (must be in the allowlist)

tools.name: read-command

tools.description: Read recent output from a background session (e.g., tail -f logs).

lines.description: Number of recent lines to read

tools.name: read-session-output

tools.description: Execute an arbitrary shell command on the remote server. May modify the system. Commands classified destructive or privileged go through the approval gate; approvalPolicy on the profile decides whether that is a prompt, an automatic allow, or a refusal. Single-line only: a command containing a line break is refused, so upload a multi-line script with sftp-upload and run it by path.

session.description: Run in an existing interactive session (stateful)

tools.name: run-command

tools.description: Download a file from the remote server via SFTP.
tools.name: sftp-download

tools.description: Upload a file to the remote server via SFTP (secure file transfer, not shell-based).
tools.name: sftp-upload

tools.description: Send a signal (INT, TERM, KILL) to a remote process by PID.
tools.name: signal-process
